limitation: These minimized guards protect six named correctness failures found during a purposive three-project review. They are not a representative accuracy benchmark.

cases.observedFailure: A static @Controller({ path, version }) prefix was treated as dynamic and method routes were emitted at incorrect root paths.
cases.protectedContract: Static NestJS controller option paths and path arrays contribute their declared prefix.
cases.remainingBoundary: Computed option values remain dynamic and must not be guessed.

cases.observedFailure: A dynamic controller prefix could be dropped while the method-only suffix was emitted as an apparently exact route.
cases.protectedContract: An unresolved NestJS controller prefix produces path null instead of a guessed method-only path.
cases.remainingBoundary: The analyzer does not evaluate arbitrary TypeScript expressions to recover dynamic decorator values.

cases.observedFailure: An unrelated unresolved local import polluted the framework route coverage status.
cases.protectedContract: Only route-relevant structural resolution failures can make Express route coverage incomplete.
cases.remainingBoundary: A mount, router or handler relationship that is relevant and unresolved must still produce partial coverage.

cases.observedFailure: A route-handler re-export through a project alias could disappear without route-specific incomplete evidence.
cases.protectedContract: Unresolved Next.js route-handler re-exports produce next_route_handler_export_unresolved and partial coverage.
cases.remainingBoundary: Cross-module handler re-export resolution is not stable coverage in v0.6.0.

cases.observedFailure: Framework reason counts could exceed the affected-input count exposed by report-v3 coverage.
cases.protectedContract: Route coverage reason counts reconcile to affected input files instead of internal relationship-event volume.
cases.remainingBoundary: A reason count is an affected-input count, not a number of missing routes.

cases.observedFailure: Express router.all was treated as read-only even though the handler accepts state-changing HTTP methods.
cases.protectedContract: ALL is conservatively state-changing and receives state-change review reasons when controls are unresolved.
cases.remainingBoundary: Static analysis does not know which HTTP methods a handler may reject internally.
